access-decisions.words: decides who may read or do what

accounts.words: keeps accounts for people or services

audit-records.words: writes audit records of its own events

audit-store.words: stores, protects or reviews audit records

authenticators.words: issues, holds or checks authenticators (keys, tokens, certificates, passkeys)

backup-restore.words: keeps state that must be backed up and restored

boundary-traffic.words: controls traffic that crosses a network or air-gap boundary

change-path.words: is the path by which changes reach the system

crypto-module-login.words: is a cryptographic module that needs an operator login

development.words: is developed or rebuilt here, so the development process covers it

external-service.words: is, or reaches, a service outside your organization

federation.words: accepts sign-ins from another identity provider

hardware.words: is hardware, or carries hardware into a site

host-hardening.words: runs on hosts whose kernel settings it controls

identity-proofing.words: registers people after their identity is checked

integrity-checks.words: detects unauthorized software or changes automatically

labels.words: reads or enforces security labels on information

malicious-code-checks.words: scans or refuses software for malicious content

network-traffic.words: sends or receives information over a network

organization-data.words: stores your organization's information at rest

our-code.words: is code this repository writes or rebuilds

outside-users.words: admits people from outside your organization

pki-trust.words: validates certificates or keys against a trust store

privileged-remote.words: takes privileged commands over a remote connection

process-isolation.words: runs work in isolated processes or containers

re-authentication.words: asks a signed-in person to sign in again before an action

remote-access.words: is the entry point for remote access

shared-resources.words: shares memory, storage or nodes between people

sign-in.words: signs people in or admits them only after a sign-in

sign-in-page.words: is the page where people sign in

software.words: is software or firmware we ship or deploy

software-installation.words: controls which software may be installed or run

supplier-process.words: carries the supplier's own policies, procedures, plans and records

time-source.words: sets the clocks of the nodes

traffic-limits.words: limits request rates or resource use against overload

two-person-control.words: needs two people for an action

user-interface.words: shows a user interface or runs code in a browser or editor

access-decisions.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: Kubernetes RBAC decides what each workload and administrator may do.

accounts.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: Kubernetes service accounts and role bindings for every site part.

admin-separation.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: cluster administration runs through the Kubernetes API, separate from workloads.

audit-records.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: RKE2 is installed with an audit policy (the Kubernetes audit log).

authenticators.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: the API server checks client certificates and service account tokens.

backup-restore.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: the cluster's etcd snapshots restore the site (47-27 recovery order).

boundary-traffic.basis: components/rke2.json: Canal networking and network policies decide traffic between pods and out of the cluster.

certificate-issuing.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: RKE2 issues the cluster's internal component certificates; site certificates are cert-manager's.

change-path.basis: resources.json tool:helm: every site part is installed and updated on the cluster through helm.

cryptography.basis: components/rke2.json: RKE2 in its FIPS build, with secrets encryption.

device-identity.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: each node joins with its own node identity.

host-hardening.basis: components/rke2.json: the CIS profile sets the node kernel settings.

monitoring.basis: resources.json image:quay.io/prometheus/node-exporter: node and cluster metrics for site monitoring.

name-resolution.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: CoreDNS resolves names inside the cluster.

network-traffic.basis: components/rke2.json: Canal networking carries every pod's traffic.

organization-data.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: etcd holds the site's Kubernetes objects and secrets at rest (secrets encryption).

pki-trust.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: the API server trusts its own cluster CA.

privileged-remote.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: administrators reach the Kubernetes API remotely for privileged commands.

process-isolation.basis: components/rke2.json: Kubernetes runs each workload in its own container and namespace.

remote-access.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: the Kubernetes API is the remote entry point for administration.

separation-of-duties.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: RBAC roles split cluster duties.

shared-resources.basis: components/rke2.json: nodes are shared between many people's sessions.

sign-in.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: administrators sign in to the API server.

software.basis: components/rke2.json: RKE2 is software every site runs.

software-installation.basis: resources.json tool:helm and image-registry: only the signed images the registry admits are run.

time-source.basis: exchanges.json time-source: the site time source sets the cluster nodes' clocks.

traffic-limits.basis: resources.json tool:rke2: resource quotas and limits on every workload.

access-decisions.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch: OpenSearch decides who may read the logs.

accounts.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch: log readers' accounts, from Keycloak.

admin-separation.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch: log administration is separate from reading.

audit-records.basis: resources.json image:cr.fluentbit.io/fluent/fluent-bit: its own shipping events.

audit-store.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch: the site's log and audit store.

backup-restore.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch: the log store must be backed up and restored.

cryptography.basis: resources.json image:cr.fluentbit.io/fluent/fluent-bit: ships logs over TLS.

integrity-checks.basis: resources.json image:quay.io/prometheus/alertmanager: alerts on the rules of deploy/values/prometheus-alerts.yaml.

monitoring.basis: resources.json image:quay.io/prometheus/prometheus and image:quay.io/prometheus/alertmanager: metrics, alert rules and alert email.

network-traffic.basis: resources.json image:cr.fluentbit.io/fluent/fluent-bit: sends logs from every node.

organization-data.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch: logs of your organization's activity at rest.

pki-trust.basis: resources.json image:cr.fluentbit.io/fluent/fluent-bit: checks the log store's TLS against the site CA.

sign-in.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch: readers sign in through Keycloak.

software.basis: components/site-logging.json: OpenSearch, Fluent Bit and Prometheus are software every site runs.

site-storage.role: The encrypted storage class for workspaces and service data (Longhorn reference class).

audit-store.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/longhornio/longhorn-manager: the log store's volumes are Longhorn volumes.

backup-restore.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/longhornio/csi-snapshotter: volume snapshots used for restores.

network-traffic.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/longhornio/longhorn-engine: keeps volume copies on other nodes in step over the network.

organization-data.basis: components/site-storage.json: the encrypted storage class for workspaces and service data.

shared-resources.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/longhornio/longhorn-share-manager: volumes several pods use at once.

software.basis: components/site-storage.json: Longhorn is software every site runs.

two-person-control.basis: resources.json image:docker.io/longhornio/longhorn-ui: deleting volumes is an operator action your organization may require two people for.

theia-cloud.role: The Theia Cloud operator, service, conversion webhook and landing page that start each person their workspace.

access-decisions.basis: resources.json chart:theia-cloud: the service starts a session only for the signed-in person who owns it.

accounts.basis: resources.json chart:theia-cloud-crds: Theia Cloud keeps workspace records per person; the accounts are Keycloak's.

admin-separation.basis: resources.json chart:theia-cloud-base: cluster-wide pieces are installed by the operator, separate from people's sessions.

audit-records.basis: resources.json image:registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/openjdk-21-runtime: the operator and service log session starts and stops.

authenticators.basis: resources.json chart:theia-cloud: the service checks the person's bearer token from Keycloak.

cryptography.basis: resources.json chart:theia-cloud-crds: the conversion webhook and service answer over TLS.

development.basis: resources.json image:registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/openjdk-21: we rebuild the operator, service and webhook from source.

network-traffic.basis: resources.json chart:theia-cloud: the landing page and service answer over the network.

our-code.basis: resources.json image:registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/nodejs-22: our rebuilt landing page and settings.

pki-trust.basis: resources.json chart:theia-cloud-crds: the conversion webhook's CA bundle from cert-manager.

process-isolation.basis: resources.json chart:theia-cloud: one workbench session per person in its own pod.

remote-access.basis: resources.json image:registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/nginx-126: the landing page where a signed-in person opens their workbench.

sessions.basis: resources.json image:registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/openjdk-21-runtime: starts, tracks and stops each person's workbench session.

shared-resources.basis: resources.json chart:theia-cloud: sessions share the site nodes with limits per session.

sign-in.basis: resources.json chart:theia-cloud: the landing page needs a signed-in person.

software.basis: components/theia-cloud.json: the operator, service, webhook and landing page are software every site runs.

traffic-limits.basis: deploy/values/theia-cloud.yaml: sessionsPerUser 1, one session per person.

unauthenticated-entry.basis: resources.json image:registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/nginx-126: the landing page is reached first and sends people to sign in.

user-interface.basis: resources.json image:registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/nginx-126: the landing page runs in the browser.

workbench.role: The Sterling workbench image that a hosted site runs for each person.

access-decisions.basis: components/workbench.json and workbench/extension/src/node/egress-contribution.ts: the workbench reuses the extension's gate and allows egress only to policy-listed servers.

accounts.basis: workbench/extension/src/common/session-identity.ts: the session runs as the signed-in person; the account itself is Keycloak's.

admin-separation.basis: workbench/extension/src/common/key-service.ts: signing needs the step-up role (sterling-workbench-stepup) that an ordinary session does not hold.

audit-records.basis: workbench/extension/src/browser/session-activity-frontend-module.ts and the extension gate log inside the image record the session's own events.

authenticators.basis: workbench/extension/src/common/secret-store.ts and key-service.ts: the person's secrets and keys sit at their own OpenBao path, never in the image.

boundary-traffic.basis: workbench/extension/src/node/egress-contribution.ts and exchanges.json model-servers and open-vsx: the session reaches only policy-listed model servers and the site extension mirror.

cryptography.basis: workbench/extension/src/common/key-service.ts: signing through OpenBao's transit keys; TLS to OpenBao and the model servers.

development.basis: components/workbench.json: the Sterling workbench image is built in this repository (workbench/Dockerfile) by the release pipeline.

device-identity.basis: workbench/extension/src/common/identity.ts: the session is bound to the person's identity rather than a device; the node identity is RKE2's.

external-service.basis: exchanges.json model-servers: workbench sessions send prompts to the model servers your organization's signed policy lists.

host-hardening.basis: workbench/Dockerfile: the image runs as a non-root user on UBI 9 minimal; the node kernel settings are RKE2's.

labels.basis: workbench reuses the extension's label handling (src/domain/gate/labels.ts) inside the image; 48.1-19 states ac-16 on it.

malicious-code-checks.basis: resources.json tool:grype: the Release workflow scans the workbench image SBOM for known vulnerabilities before publishing.

monitoring.basis: workbench/extension/src/browser/session-activity-frontend-module.ts: the session reports activity that the site's monitoring and Theia Cloud read.

network-traffic.basis: exchanges.json model-servers and open-vsx: the session sends and receives over the network, over TLS.

organization-data.basis: workbench/extension/src/browser/sterling-work-areas-module.ts and site-storage volumes: each person's workspace holds your organization's files.

our-code.basis: components/workbench.json: the workbench extension and image are written in this repository (workbench/).

pki-trust.basis: workbench/extension/src/node/backend-service.ts: TLS to OpenBao and the model servers is checked against the site CA.

process-isolation.basis: components/theia-cloud.json: each person gets their own workbench container, which Theia Cloud starts and RKE2 isolates.

re-authentication.basis: workbench/extension/src/common/key-service.ts: signing checks acr and auth_time and sends the person to step up first.

sessions.basis: workbench/extension/src/common/session-identity.ts and session-activity.ts: the session view, its activity tracker and its retry.

shared-resources.basis: components/workbench.json: many people's workbench containers share the site nodes and storage that RKE2 and site-storage separate.

sign-in.basis: workbench/extension/src/browser/session-identity-frontend-module.ts: the session admits only the person oauth2-proxy signed in.

software.basis: components/workbench.json: the Sterling workbench image is software a hosted site runs.

software-installation.basis: exchanges.json open-vsx: the workbench installs extensions only from the site Open VSX mirror.

user-interface.basis: components/workbench.json: the workbench is the browser editor each person uses.
